topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by connecting it to the practicals and outlining its learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how investigations of cancer-causing viruses established that transformation can originate in altered cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental testing of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether a gene or mutation transforms cells.

topics.label: Functional interpretation of cancer genes and mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how a mutation's effects on protein activity and cellular regulation determine its role in promoting or restraining cancer.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures of genome maintenance generate genetic instability and alter cancer-cell behavior.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutation acquisition influences the progression from normal colorectal tissue to metastatic cancer.

topics.label: Inherited tumor-suppressor mutations and the course of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how inherited tumor-suppressor defects predispose to cancer, with BRCA2 restoration illustrating why an established tumor can remain malignant after a defect is corrected.

topics.label: Closing, further reading, and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with an invitation for questions, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
